 CHIEF JUSTICE ROBERTS:  We will hear
 argument this morning in Case 25-459, Salazar
 versus Paramount Global.
 Mr. Hammack.
 ORAL ARGUMENT OF JOSHUA I. HAMMACK
 ON BEHALF OF THE PETITIONER
 MR. HAMMACK: Mr. Chief Justice, and
may it please the Court:
 Outraged by the disclosure of one
 person's video-watching history, Congress
 enacted the Video Privacy Protection Act.  In
 Section (b)(1), the Act provides for civil
liability when a video tape service provider
knowingly discloses personally identifiable
information concerning any consumer of such
 provider.
 The Act defines three of those terms.
At bottom, a video tape service provider is the
kind of entity that will owe obligations under
 the law.  Personally identifiable information
is the kind of information the statute protects
in (b)(1)(D) and (E). And a consumer is the
 kind of person whose information is protected

in Section (b)(1).  The Act permits disclosures
with a consumer's consent, and in 2013,
Congress made that consent easier to obtain,
online, in advance, for up to two years.
 Here, Paramount Global systematically
discloses personally identifiable information
 to Facebook without obtaining consent.  These
 are not one-off disclosures.  They happen
constantly, instantly, every time someone,
including a consumer, watches a video on the
 website.  Paramount has shaped its business
 around these disclosures.
 All it needed to avoid liability was
its consumers' consent, something it and
 Facebook agree was easy to get.  Paramount just
didn't get it. So it asks this Court to narrow
the law by imposing an audiovisual limitation
on the phrase "goods or services" in the
 definition of "consumer."
 But Congress put audiovisual
limitations where it wanted them, in the
definitions of both "video tape service
 provider" and "personally identifiable
information," not in the definition of
 "consumer."  That choice is dispositive.

natural to think that goods or services from a

 video-related services?

 cassette tapes or similar audiovisual

 video materials or services.  That's a second

 definition, we have goods or services.

coming from a video tape service provider.
That they're different tells us that a provider
 can do all three things.  It can engage in
transactions concerning all three.

 former colleague, Justice Breyer, confronted
 with questions like this, you know, his
favorite hypothetical in that area anyway was a

any consumer" is a second. And the reading, I
